summary: IDS feed s062_single is degraded due to 28.9% duplicate packets (864/2989), well above 5% threshold. All other visibility checks (one-way, truncation, drops, overload, encryption, VLAN, tunnels, oversize) are healthy.

findings.root_cause: Packet broker is forwarding duplicate copies of the same packets to the IDS - typically caused by aggregating both directions of a SPAN/mirror or two TAP feeds covering the same link without deduplication, or SPAN configured to mirror both ingress and egress on the same VLAN.
findings.impact_on_tool: IDS wastes CPU/capacity processing 28.9% redundant traffic, inflates connection state and alert counts, risks duplicate alerts and missed detections due to state-table pressure and inefficient signature matching despite needing full payload and bidirectional visibility.

recommended_fix.why: Enable packet-broker deduplication to drop identical packets seen within a short time window before delivery to the 1 Gbps IDS port, restoring capacity for unique traffic inspection.
